slides.alt: A long passenger steamship lies completely on its side in a narrow city river, its dark hull exposed above the waterline. A few small figures stand on the upturned hull, and brick warehouses line the shore.
slides.credit: National Archives and Records Administration, NAID 281841

slides.alt: A tall white excursion steamship with two funnels and several decks sits upright at a city dock. Overlay text reads '2,500 people on board'.
slides.credit: National Archives and Records Administration, NAID 281840

slides.alt: A dramatic black-and-white newspaper drawing shows a large steamship tilting sharply toward the water as tiny figures scramble on its decks. Overlay text reads 'Then it went over'.
slides.credit: Bob Satterfield, The Tacoma Times, July 27, 1915

slides.alt: A huge dark hull fills the frame at water level, seen from a boat on the river. Overlay text reads '20 feet of water'.
Dozens of people stand on the exposed side of a capsized steamship while small rowboats crowd the water around it. Overlay text reads '844 died'.
slides.credit: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division, George Grantham Bain Collection

slides.alt: A wide sepia photograph shows a city river crowded with boats and onlookers, with the exposed hull of a capsized steamship beside a bridge. Overlay text reads 'Raised in two weeks'.
slides.credit: Kaufmann, Weimer & Fabry Co., Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division

slides.alt: Dark closing card with the Cluefolio logo, the message 'Everything you were never told. Every day.', and a button reading FOLLOW @CLUEFOLIO.
